'''Gerald Enoch Sacks''' (1933 – October 4, 2019) was an American [[logician]] whose most important contributions were in [[recursion theory]]. Named after him is [[Sacks forcing]], a [[forcing (mathematics)|forcing]] notion based on [[perfect set]]s<ref>{{citation|title=Combinatorial Set Theory: With a Gentle Introduction to Forcing|series=Springer Monographs in Mathematics|first=Lorenz J.|last=Halbeisen|publisher=Springer|year=2011|isbn=9781447121732|pages=380–381|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NZVb54INnywC&pg=PA380}}.</ref> and the Sacks Density Theorem, which asserts that the [[partial order]] of the [[recursively enumerable]] [[Turing degree]]s is [[dense order|dense]].<ref>{{citation|title=Recursively Enumerable Sets and Degrees: A Study of Computable Functions and Computably Generated Sets|series=Perspectives in Mathematical Logic|first=Robert I.|last=Soare|publisher=Springer|year=1987|isbn=9783540152996|page=245|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9I7Pl00LU5gC&pg=PA245}}.</ref> Sacks had a joint appointment as a professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and at [[Harvard University]] starting in 1972 and became emeritus at M.I.T. in 2006 and at Harvard in 2012.<ref>[http://www.math.harvard.edu/~sacks/Short%20CV.pdf Short CV], retrieved 2015-06-26.</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://math.mit.edu/news/integral/integral_2006.pdf|journal=Integral: News from the Mathematics Department at MIT|page=6|title=Professor Gerald Sacks Retires from MIT|date=Autumn 2006|volume=1}}.</ref><ref>Chi Tat Chong, Yue Yang, "An interview with Gerald E. Sacks", ''Recursion Theory: Computational Aspects of Definability'', {{isbn|3110275643}}, 2015, [https://books.google.com/books?id=_axUCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA275&lpg=PA275 p. 275]</ref>

Sacks was born in [[Brooklyn]] in 1933.  He earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1961 from [[Cornell University]] under the direction of [[J. Barkley Rosser]], with his dissertation ''On Suborderings of Degrees of Recursive Insolvability''. Among his notable students are [[Lenore Blum]], [[Harvey Friedman (mathematician)|Harvey Friedman]], [[Sy Friedman]], [[Leo Harrington]], [[Richard Shore]], [[Steve Simpson (mathematician)|Steve Simpson]] and [[Theodore Slaman]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy |id=22616}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* [https://books.google.com/books/about/Degrees_of_Unsolvability.html?id=ZXEJGn_T0A4C Degrees of unsolvability], Princeton University Press 1963, 1966<ref>Review of ''Degrees of unsolvability'' by [[Kenneth Appel]], {{MR|0186554}}</ref>
* ''Saturated Model Theory'', Benjamin 1972; [https://books.google.com/books/about/Saturated_Model_Theory_2nd_Edition.html?id=xLFI9fOozVoC 2nd edition], World Scientific 2010<ref>Review of ''Saturated model theory'' by P. Stepanek, {{MR|0398817}}</ref>
* ''Higher Recursion theory'', Springer 1990<ref>Review of ''Higher recursion theory'' by Dag Normann, {{MR|1080970}}</ref>
* ''Selected Logic Papers'', World Scientific 1999<ref>Review of ''Selected logic papers'' by Dag Normann, {{MR|1783306}}</ref>
* ''Mathematical Logic in the 20th Century'', World Scientific 2003
